items.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: when he left home he didn’t know whether it was a rock ‘n roll, whether it was with Stravinsky, whether it was with Barbra Streisand, he didn’t, or with a — he didn’t know who it was for.

ctx.x: Well I didn’t mean that to say in a way that he would relax and say oh I’m there, I don’t really have to work anymore, but when he began to get some feedback from other musicians, that hey, you’re doing it.

Oh, I think he got that always. In the Calloway band, and then — I’ll tell you what happened — he came to New York after he left Calloway’s band, and he was walking down the street one day and he ran into Jackie Gleason and his manager Bull. So Jackie, well Milton knew Jackie when he was, when only the musicians were laughing at his jokes, when they used to buy him a drink, so but he, as I said the day he ran into Milton he said to Milton said, “well what are you doing.” And Milton says, “well I’m looking for a…

things that got him started. And once they knew that he was qualified, he could read anything, play anything, and so he just started getting more work than he could handle. And then there for a long time, Osie Johnson the drummer, Barry Galbraith, the guitar player, Hank Jones the piano player, and Milton, they would work, they would do at least three sessions a day — 10-1, 2-5 and 7-8 every day. They were called the New York, the New York Rhythm Section. And they did that for years. As I say that’s because they…
